title: What Is a $45 per Hour Annual Salary? A Full Breakdown for 2026–27
description: Find out the $45 per hour annual salary for a 38‑hour week, plus fortnightly pay, tax, super, and how it compares to the National Minimum Wage and award rates.
salarySummary: At $45 per hour for a 38‑hour week, the annual salary is $88,920, with a fortnightly gross of $3,420 and an estimated net of about $69,946 after tax and Medicare.

faqs.q: How do I calculate the annual salary from $45 per hour?
faqs.a: Multiply $45 by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52. For a standard 38‑hour week: $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. This formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is the take‑home pay for a $45 per hour annual salary?
faqs.a: Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the 2% Medicare levy, the estimated annual net pay is about $69,946. This is after $17,196 in income tax and $1,778 in Medicare. The estimate uses the full tax‑free threshold and does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary sacrifice.

faqs.q: How does $45 per hour compare to the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 casual including 25% loading). At $45 per hour, you earn well above the minimum. Award rates vary by industry and classification; $45 may be above or below the award rate for your job. Check your specific award or enterprise agreement for the correct minimum. The figure here is not a job median – it is simply a rate used for illustration.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the $45 per Hour Annual Salary

If you earn **$45 per hour** and work a standard 38‑hour week, your annual salary before tax is **$88,920**. This is calculated using the formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For this article we assume a 38‑hour week, which is the ordinary full‑time hours used by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. If your actual hours differ, simply replace 38 with your weekly hours. The result is an estimate – it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

### Fortnightly Pay from $45 per Hour

A fortnight is two weeks. At 38 hours per week, your fortnightly gross pay is:

$45 × 38 × 2 = **$3,420**

Many employers pay fortnightly, so this figure can help you budget. Your net fortnightly pay after tax and Medicare will be lower – see the tax section below.

### Tax on a $45 per Hour Annual Salary

For the 2026–27 income year, the Australian Tax Office resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on the excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed here).

On $88,920:
- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on next $26,800 (up to $45,000): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on remaining $43,920 (up to $88,920): 30% = $13,176
- Total income tax: $17,196
- Medicare levy: 2% × $88,920 = $1,778.40
- Total tax and Medicare: $18,974.40
- **Estimated net annual pay: $69,945.60**

This is an estimate only. Your actual tax may differ if you have deductions, offsets, HELP debt, or the Medicare levy surcharge.

### Superannuation on $45 per Hour

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid **on top** of your salary. For $88,920, the annual super contribution is:

12% × $88,920 = **$10,670.40**

This amount goes into your super fund and is not included in your take‑home pay. The super guarantee is capped at the maximum contribution base of $270,830 (2026–27), so your full earnings are below that limit. For more on super and packaging, see our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### How $45 per Hour Compares to Minimum and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is **$26.44 per hour** for a 38‑hour week, or **$1,004.90 per week**. Casual employees receive an additional 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate **$33.05 per hour**. At $45 per hour, you are earning well above the minimum.

However, many industries have award rates that are higher than the national minimum. For example, some classifications in the Building and Construction Award or the Hospitality Award may be above $45. The figure of $45 per hour is not a job median – it is simply a rate used for this example. If you want to check the correct minimum for your job, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Casual Loading and the $45 per Hour Rate

If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate is typically lower than the permanent rate, and you receive a 25% casual loading on top. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** into a calculator – always start with the base rate. For $45 per hour base, the casual rate including loading would be $56.25 per hour. Our [timesheet](/) has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading automatically.

### Average Earnings Context

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), full‑time adult ordinary time earnings averaged **$2,083.70 per week**, which is about $54.31 per hour for a 38‑hour week. All employees total earnings (including part‑time) averaged **$1,579.20 per week**. At $45 per hour, you are below the full‑time average but above the all‑employees average. Remember these are averages, not medians for any specific job.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Own Rate

To calculate your own annual salary, fortnightly pay, tax, and super, use our [timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading), select your weekly hours (default 38), and the tool will show the annual gross, net, super, and tax estimates. You can also toggle casual loading to see the effect.

### Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax‑free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
